matrix.t: The evaluation set again: **100 emails**, rows are actual, columns are predicted, and spam is the positive class. **TP = 16, FN = 4, FP = 8, TN = 72.**

predicted-positive-column.t: Precision looks **only at the emails the filter flagged** as spam. That is the predicted-spam **column** of the matrix: 16 + 8 = **24** emails.

select-tp.t: Of the 24 flagged emails, **16 really are spam**: the true positives.

select-fp.t: The other **8** flagged emails are legitimate: false positives, **good mail blocked by mistake**.

precision-question.t: Precision asks one question: **when the model says spam, how often is it right?**

numerator.t: The numerator counts the flagged emails that really are spam: **TP = 16**.

denominator.t: The denominator is **all predicted positives**, the whole predicted-spam column: **TP + FP = 24**. Notice that it is not all of the spam.

calculate.t: **Precision = TP / (TP + FP) = 16 / 24, about 0.667.** One more check against the matrix: 24 emails were flagged.

interpret.t: Two out of every three emails the filter blocks really are spam; **one in three is legitimate**. Precision says nothing about spam that was never flagged: that question is answered by recall.
